feedback: Decision: approve. The candidate is the best raced design (iteration 6, score 372.74: kd 0.40, kp 3.0, ki 0.30, base_speed 1.5, sensor x = ±0.032 m, footprint 0.016 m) with one change, kp 3.0 to 3.25. That is a single-variable step, and the candidate correctly rejects the kd 0.50 result (iteration 8, score 352.73, oval finishes 18 of 20, s-bend progress down from 0.319 to 0.226). It also correctly keeps base_speed 1.5, since speed 1.3 cut oval finishes from 19 to 7 (iteration 7). The evidence against kp is iteration 2 (kp 3.5, score 99.25), but that run used the narrower ±0.024 m spread, where line losses were already high. At ±0.032 m the sensors give earlier warning, so a modest kp increase is a reasonable test. The candidate is valid: all values are inside the contract, the weights are antisymmetric, and line_loss is last_direction. I make no claim about how it will perform. Two iterations remain, so racing now gives the telemetry that matters most. Read the race as follows. If oval finishes stay at 17 or more and the score holds at or above 372.74, keep kp 3.25 as the new best. If oval finishes fall below 17, or the score falls below 372.74, revert to kp 3.0 with kd 0.40, which is the best raced design. In either case, the next lever is the outer sensor spread, since widening from ±0.024 to ±0.032 m was the largest single gain (oval finishes 3 to 7, s-bend line losses 2.0 to 1.05, iterations 3 to 5). Keep kd 0.40 and ki 0.30 unless the race shows a clear reason to change them.
requested_changes: Keep kp 3.25 only if oval finishes stay at 17 or more of 20 and the score holds at or above 372.74 (iteration 6). Otherwise revert kp to 3.0, since kp 3.5 at the narrower spread (iteration 2, score 99.25) showed higher oval line-loss events.
Keep kd 0.40, ki 0.30 and base_speed 1.5 in this step. kd 0.50 lowered the score (iteration 8, 352.73, oval finishes 19 to 18), and base_speed 1.3 cut oval finishes from 19 to 7 (iteration 7).

If the score holds, the next single-variable test is the outer sensors at x = ±0.040 m with the best kp and kd, since widening from ±0.024 to ±0.032 m cut oval line losses from 1.7 to 1.2 and raised finishes from 3 to 7 (iterations 3 to 5). Only test this if the race leaves at least two runs.
